title: Office of Postsecondary Education ID Number Institution information
description:
Office of Postsecondary Education ID Number Institution information
Office of Postsecondary Education identification number for those
institutions eligible to participate in Title IV programs
Title IV Eligible: Institution is eligible to participate in Title IV
federal financial aid programs (i.e. Pell Grants, SEOG, Stafford Loans, 
Perkins Loans etc.) For an institution to be eligible to participate in 
Title IV financial aid programs it must offer a program of at least 300 
clock hours in length, have accreditation recognized by the 
U.S. Department of Education, have been in business for at least 2 years,
and have signed a participation agreement with the Department.
Needy students attending Title IV institutions may qualify for 
federal aid--e.g., Pell grants and Perkins loans.

title: OPE Title IV eligibility indicator code Institution information
description:
OPE Title IV eligibility indicator code Institution information
OPE Title IV eligibility indicator code identifies insitutions that are eligible
to participate in Title IV federal financial aid programs. It identifies 
institutions as follows:
1 - Participates in Title IV federal financial aid programs 
2 - Branch campus of a main campus that participates in Title IV 
3 - Deferment only - limited participation  
4 - New participants that became eligible to participate during the fall
     the fall  collection period 
5 - Institutions not currently participating in Title IV programs but has an 
     OPE Identification number on the data file  
6 - Institution not currently participating in Title IV programs and does not
 have  an OPE Identification number on the data file.
Related glossary links.
Title IV Eligible: Institution is eligible to participate in Title IV
federal financial aid programs (i.e. Pell Grants, SEOG, Stafford Loans, 
Perkins Loans etc.) For an institution to be eligible to participate in 
Title IV financial aid programs it must offer a program of at least 300 
clock hours in length, have accreditation recognized by the 
U.S. Department of Education, have been in business for at least 2 years,
and have signed a participation agreement with the Department.
Needy students attending Title IV institutions may qualify for 
federal aid--e.g., Pell grants and Perkins loans.

codes.1: Participates in Title IV federal financial aid programs
codes.2: Branch campus of a main campus that participates  in Title IV
codes.4: New participants (became eligible during the fall collection period)
codes.5: Not currently participating in Title IV, has an OPE ID number
codes.6: Not currently participating in Title IV, does not have OPE ID number

title: Status of institution Institution status information
description:
Status of institution Institution status information
Current status information of active (open,new) and
inactive (closed, mergers, etc)  institutions that were
ever included in the IPEDS data base since 1990
A - Active - institution active and not an add
C - Combined - merged with another institution
D - Delete - institution is out of business
H - Area search on hold pending verification
I - Inactive
M - Death with data - closed in current yr
N - New - added during the current year
O - Out-of-scope - not within scope of universe
P - Potential add - might be added
Q - Potential restore - might be restored
R - Restore - restored to the current universe
S - Split - split into more than one institution
U - Duplicate - UNITID previously assigned
W - Wipe out - out-of-scope potential add
X - Potential restore not within scope of IPEDS
Z - Universe III - out-of-scope

codes.A: Active - institution active and not an add
codes.M: Death with data - closed in current yr
codes.N: New - added during the current year
codes.R: Restore - restored to the current universe
codes.S: Split - split into more than one institution

title: Institution is active in current year Insitutition status information
description:
Institution is active in current year Insitutition status information
This variable indicates whether an institution was active (open) during
the Fall/Spring data collection (Fall 2000).  If an institution closed in the
fall 2000 and was open for academic year 1999-2000, it would still be
considered active so that completions,  finance,  and financial aid data
can be collected.  These insititutions are identified by  ACT variable which
gives more detail on the status of an instititution.
1=Active
2=Not active.

title: Parent/child allocation method - Finance
description:
The following methods were used to create the factors to allocate combined finance (revenues, expenses, grants and endowments) data across each separately identified parent and child institution:

Student FTE – This is a proportion of student FTE for a specific school to the sum of the student FTE for all the schools (parent and children).  This method uses data reported by the institutions on the 2004 Enrollment component.

Faculty/staff FTE from the 2004 Fall Staff component – This is a proportion of total staff FTE for a specific school to the sum of the total staff FTE for all the schools (parent and children).  This method uses data reported by the institutions on the 2004 Fall Staff component.  FTE is calculated by adding full-time staff to 1/3 of part-time staff.

Faculty/staff FTE from the 2004 EAP component – This is a proportion of total staff FTE for a specific school to the sum of the total staff FTE for all the schools (parent and children).  This method uses data reported by the institutions on the 2004 Employees by Assigned Position component.  FTE is calculated by adding full-time staff to 1/3 of part-time staff.

Faculty/staff FTE from the 2003 Fall Staff component – This is a proportion of total staff FTE for a specific school to the sum of the total staff FTE for all the schools (parent and children).  This method uses data reported by the institutions on the 2003 Fall Staff component.  FTE is calculated by adding full-time staff to 1/3 of part-time staff.

Full-time faculty from the 2004 Fall Staff component – This is a proportion of total full-time faculty for a specific school to the sum of the total full-time faculty for all the schools (parent and children).  This method uses data reported by the institutions on the 2004 Fall Staff component.

Equal shares determined by the number of schools in the reporting relationship – This is a proportion dividing 1 by the total number of schools (parent and children).

Submitted by parent institution – This is a proportion submitted by the parent institution for all the schools (parent and children).

codes.1: Student FTE
codes.2: Faculty/staff FTE from the 2004 Fall Staff component
codes.3: Faculty/staff FTE from the 2004 EAP component
codes.4: Faculty/staff FTE from the 2003 Fall Staff component
codes.5: Full-time faculty from the 2004 EAP component
codes.8: Equal shares determined by the number of schools in the reporting relationship

title: Parent/child system indicator - Finance
description:
Identifies the type of parent/child relationship for the system

1=Full parent child system - All children campuses (PRCH_F=2) finance data are reported by the Parent institution (PRCH_F=1) as identified by the IDX_F variable (Unitid reporting finance data)

2=Partial child system (1) – Has children campuses (PRCH_F=3) that report their own current funds, revenues and expenses, but assets, liabilities and other system wide information are reported by the parent institution (PRCH_F=1) as identified by the IDX_F variable. Can include children institutions (PRCH_F=2) that report all finance data with the parent institution.

3=Partial child system (2) -  Has children campuses (PRCH_F=3) that report their own current funds, revenues and expenses, but assets, liabilities and other system wide information are reported by the parent institution (PRCH_F=1)  as identified by the IDX_F variable.  This Partial system will include one or more child campus (PRCH_F=2)  whose current funds revenues and expenses are reported by one of the partial campuses. In this case the IDX_F variable for this child campus will have the UNITID of the reporting partial campus. Partial reporting children campuses that also act as a parent institution for other child campuses are identied as (PRCH_F=6).

5 – Partial child system of a non IPEDS institution.  These campuses only report revenues and expenses, but assets, liabilities and other system wide information are reported by an entity that is out of the scope of IPEDS, such as a hospital or state local training centers.

codes.1: Full parent/child system
codes.2: Partial parent child system (1)
codes.5: System with partial reporting children campuses of NON-IPEDS entity

title: Parent/child system indicator - Finance
description:
Identifies the type of parent/child relationship for the system

1=Full parent child system - All children campuses (PRCH_F=2) finance data are reported by the Parent institution (PRCH_F=1) as identified by the IDX_F variable (Unitid reporting finance data)

2=Partial child system (1) – Has children campuses (PRCH_F=3) that report their own current funds, revenues and expenses, but assets, liabilities and other system wide information are reported by the parent institution (PRCH_F=1) as identified by the IDX_F variable. Can include children institutions (PRCH_F=2) that report all finance data with the parent institution.

3=Partial child system (2) -  Has children campuses (PRCH_F=3) that report their own current funds, revenues and expenses, but assets, liabilities and other system wide information are reported by the parent institution (PRCH_F=1)  as identified by the IDX_F variable.  This Partial system will include one or more child campus (PRCH_F=2)  whose current funds revenues and expenses are reported by one of the partial campuses. In this case the IDX_F variable for this child campus will have the UNITID of the reporting partial campus. Partial reporting children campuses that also act as a parent institution for other child campuses are identied as (PRCH_F=6).

5 – Partial child system of a non IPEDS institution.  These campuses only report revenues and expenses, but assets, liabilities and other system wide information are reported by an entity that is out of the scope of IPEDS, such as a hospital or state local training centers.

codes.1: Full parent/child system
codes.2: Partial parent child system (1)
codes.5: System with partial reporting children campuses of NON-IPEDS entity

The child institution record will not have  data because it is included with the parent. The variable IDX_F contains the UNITID of the parent institution.

codes.1: Parent record - includes data from branch campuses
codes.2: Child record - data reported with parent campus
codes.3: Partial child record - reports revenues/expenses. Assets/liabilties reported with parent
codes.6: Partial parent/child record - reports revenues/expenses that also includes data from other branch campuses. Assets/liabilties reported with parent
codes.5: Child record - reports partial data but other data is included  with entity that is not a postsecondary institution

title: Parent/child allocation factor - Finance

title: Parent/child system indicator - Finance
description:
Identifies the type of parent/child relationship for the system

1=Full parent child system - All children campuses (PRCH_F=2) finance data are reported by the Parent institution (PRCH_F=1) as identified by the IDX_F variable (Unitid reporting finance data)

2=Partial child system (1) – Has children campuses (PRCH_F=3) that report their own current funds, revenues and expenses, but assets, liabilities and other system wide information are reported by the parent institution (PRCH_F=1) as identified by the IDX_F variable. Can include children institutions (PRCH_F=2) that report all finance data with the parent institution.

3=Partial child system (2) -  Has children campuses (PRCH_F=3) that report their own current funds, revenues and expenses, but assets, liabilities and other system wide information are reported by the parent institution (PRCH_F=1)  as identified by the IDX_F variable.  This Partial system will include one or more child campus (PRCH_F=2)  whose current funds revenues and expenses are reported by one of the partial campuses. In this case the IDX_F variable for this child campus will have the UNITID of the reporting partial campus. Partial reporting children campuses that also act as a parent institution for other child campuses are identied as (PRCH_F=6).

5 – Partial child system of a non IPEDS institution.  These campuses only report revenues and expenses, but assets, liabilities and other system wide information are reported by an entity that is out of the scope of IPEDS, such as a hospital or state local training centers.

codes.1: Full parent/child system
codes.2: Partial parent child system (1)
codes.5: System with partial reporting children campuses of NON-IPEDS entity

title: Postsecondary and Title IV institution indicator A derived variable to easily select institutions which are (1) currently in the IPEDS universe, (2) open to the public, (3) participants in Title IV program, and (4) primarily postsecondary institutions.
description:
Postsecondary and Title IV institution indicator A derived variable to easily select institutions which are (1) currently in the IPEDS universe, (2) open to the public, (3) participants in Title IV program, and (4) primarily postsecondary institutions.
This variable (PSET4FLG=1)is used to produce tables that are published in IPEDS ED Tabs and tables in the Digest of Education Statistics.

It is derived as follows:
If (opeflag in (1,2,7) and postsec=1 and openpubl=1) 
  or unitid in (128328,130624,164155,197036) then pset4flg=1
If opeflag in (3,4,5,6) and postsec=1 and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=2
If opeflag in (1,2,7) and postsec=2 and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=3
If opeflag in (3,4,5,6) and postsec=2 and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=4
If opeflag in (3,4,5,6) and postsec=1 and openpubl=2 then pset4flg=6
If cyactive=2 then pset4flg=9

NOTES: 
The four United States Service academies (Air Force, Coast Guard, Naval and Military)are also included as PSET4FLG=1, even though they are opeflag=3, deferment only. 
Schools that became eligible to participate in Title IV after the IPEDS universe was finalized for the reporting year (OPEFLAG=4) are NOT included. 
Schools that became ineligible to participate in Title IV after the IPEDS universe was finalized for the reporting year (OPEFLAG=7) are included.

title: Postsecondary and Title IV institution indicator
description:
A derived indicator to easily select institutions who are (1) currently in the IPEDS universe, (2) open to the public, (3) participant in Title IV program, and (4) primarily postsecondary institution.

This variable is used to produce tables that are published in IPEDS E.D. tabs and tables in the Digest of Education Statistics.

It is derived as follows:
If opeflag in (1 2 ) and deggrant in (1 2) and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=1
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and deggrant in (1 2) and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=2
If opeflag in (1 2 ) and deggrant in (3) and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=3
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and deggrant in (3) and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=4
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and deggrant in (1 2) and openpubl=2 then pset4flg=6
If cyactive=2 then pset4flg=9
The four United States Service Air Force, Coast Guard, Naval and Military Academies are also included as PSET4FLG=1, even though they are opeflag=3, deferment only.

codes.1: Title IV postsecondary institution
codes.2: Non-Title IV postsecondary institution
codes.3: Title IV NOT primarily postsecondary institution
codes.4: Non-Title IV NOT primarily postsecondary institution
codes.6: Non-Title IV postsecondary institution that is NOT open to the public
codes.9: Institution is not active in current universe

title: Institutional category
description:
Institutional category

This indicator was derived using the level of offerings reported on the 2004-05 Institutional Characteristics (IC) component and the number and level of awards that were reported on the 2003-04 Completions (C) component.

The following is the specific derivation:

1) Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees - These institutions offer either a Master's degree (LEVEL7), Doctor's degree (LEVEL9) or a First-professional degree (LEVEL10) and do not offer a Bachelor's degree (LEVEL5) or an Associate's degree (LEVEL3). 

2) Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a bachelor's degree (LEVEL5). Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded is greater than 50 percent. (IC and C)

3) Degree-granting, other baccalaureate granting - These institutions offer a bachelor's degree (LEVEL5). Also,  the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded must be less than or equal to 50 percent.(IC and C)

Bachelor's  degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree awarded is the sum of: 
 Bachelor's degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=5,MAJORNUM=1)
 Postbaccalaureate certificates (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=6,MAJORNUM=1)
 Master's degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=7,MAJORNUM=1)
 Post-master's certificates (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=8,MAJORNUM=1)
 Doctor's degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=9,MAJORNUM=1)
 First-professional degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=10,MAJORNUM=1)
 First-professional certificates (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=11,MAJORNUM=1)

Total degrees and certificates is the sum of:
 Bachelor degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelors degree as defined above and 
 Associate's degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=3,MAJORNUM=1)
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least two but less-than four academic years (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=4,MAJORNUM=1).
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least one but less-than two academic years (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=2,MAJORNUM=1); 
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=1,MAJORNUM=1) 

4) Degree-granting,  Associate's and certificates - Institutions offer an Associate's degree (LEVEL3) and may offer other postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year (LEVEL1); at least one but less-than two academic years (LEVEL2); at least two but less-than four academic years (LEVEL4). (IC)

5) Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's (LEVEL3), Bachelor's (LEVEL5), Master's (LEVEL7), Doctor's (LEVEL9) or First-professional (LEVEL10) degrees, but offer either Postbaccaulaureate (LEVEL6), Post-master's (LEVEL8) or First-professional (LEVEL11) certificates. (IC)

6) Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's (LEVEL3), Bachelor's (LEVEL5), Master's (LEVEL7), Doctor's (LEVEL9),  or  First-professional(LEVEL10) degrees, or certificates above the baccalaureate level(LEVEL6,LEVEL8 and LEVEL11). They do offer postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year (LEVEL1); at least one but less than two academic years (LEVEL2); or at least two but less than four academic years.(LEVEL4) (IC)

All inactive institutions (CYACTIVE in (2,3)) and administrative units (Sector=0) were coded as not applicable. Any institution that did not respond to the 2004-05 Institutional Characteristics component or the 2003-04 Completions component were coded as not reported or could not derive. These were all NonTitle IV institutions.

Additional notes on classifying Degree-granting primarily baccalaureate or above and other baccalaureate granting:

Degree-granting institutions whose completions data are reported with their parent institution were assigned the same code as the parent institution.
 
New degree-granting institutions that offer a bachelor's degree, but have not yet awarded bachelor degrees in academic year 2003-04 were assigned as follows:

  If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above (indicating the level was offered) and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above.
  
  If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's degree and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, other baccalaureate granting.
  
  For institutions that reported zeros for both bachelor's degrees or above and for levels below the bachelor's the number of programs (CIP codes) by level was used to determine the primary classification. If the number of programs with reported zeros for degrees/certificates at the bachelor's level or above was greater than the number of programs with reported zeros for degrees/certificates less than the baccalaureate, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, primarily bachelor's or above.  If the number of programs with reported zeros for degrees/certificates at the bachelor's level or above was less than the number of programs with reported zeros for degrees/certificates less than the baccalaureate, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, other baccalaureate granting.

codes.1: Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees
codes.2: Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above
codes.5: Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate
codes.6: Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate

title: Postsecondary and Title IV institution indicator
description:
A derived indicator to easily select institutions who are (1) currently in the IPEDS universe, (2) open to the public, (3) participant in Title IV program, and (4) primarily postsecondary institution.

This variable is used to produce tables that are published in IPEDS E.D. tabs and tables in the Digest of Education Statistics.

It is derived as follows:
If opeflag in (1 2 ) and deggrant in (1 2) and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=1
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and deggrant in (1 2) and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=2
If opeflag in (1 2 ) and deggrant in (3) and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=3
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and deggrant in (3) and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=4
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and deggrant in (1 2) and openpubl=2 then pset4flg=6
If cyactive=2 then pset4flg=9
The four United States Service Air Force, Coast Guard, Naval and Military Academies are also included as PSET4FLG=1, even though they are opeflag=3, deferment only.

codes.1: Title IV postsecondary institution
codes.2: Non-Title IV postsecondary institution
codes.3: Title IV NOT primarily postsecondary institution
codes.6: Non-Title IV postsecondary institution that is NOT open to the public
codes.9: Institution is not active in current universe

title: Institutional category
description:
Institutional category

This indicator was derived using the level of offerings reported on the 2006-07 Institutional Characteristics (IC) component and the number and level of awards that were reported on the 2005-06 Completions (C) component.

The following is the specific derivation:

1) Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees - These institutions offer either a Master's degree (LEVEL7), Doctor's degree (LEVEL9) or a First-professional degree (LEVEL10) and do not offer a Bachelor's degree (LEVEL5) or an Associate's degree (LEVEL3). 

2) Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a bachelor's degree (LEVEL5). Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded is greater than 50 percent. (IC and C)

3) Degree-granting, other baccalaureate granting - These institutions offer a bachelor's degree (LEVEL5). Also,  the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded must be less than or equal to 50 percent.(IC and C)

Bachelor's  degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree awarded is the sum of: 
 Bachelor's degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=5,MAJORNUM=1)
 Postbaccalaureate certificates (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=6,MAJORNUM=1)
 Master's degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=7,MAJORNUM=1)
 Post-master's certificates (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=8,MAJORNUM=1)
 Doctor's degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=9,MAJORNUM=1)
 First-professional degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=10,MAJORNUM=1)
 First-professional certificates (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=11,MAJORNUM=1)

Total degrees and certificates is the sum of:
 Bachelor degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelors degree as defined above and 
 Associate's degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=3,MAJORNUM=1)
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least two but less-than four academic years (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=4,MAJORNUM=1).
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least one but less-than two academic years (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=2,MAJORNUM=1); 
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=1,MAJORNUM=1) 

4) Degree-granting,  Associate's and certificates - Institutions offer an Associate's degree (LEVEL3) and may offer other postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year (LEVEL1); at least one but less-than two academic years (LEVEL2); at least two but less-than four academic years (LEVEL4). (IC)

5) Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's (LEVEL3), Bachelor's (LEVEL5), Master's (LEVEL7), Doctor's (LEVEL9) or First-professional (LEVEL10) degrees, but offer either Postbaccaulaureate (LEVEL6), Post-master's (LEVEL8) or First-professional (LEVEL11) certificates. (IC)

6) Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's (LEVEL3), Bachelor's (LEVEL5), Master's (LEVEL7), Doctor's (LEVEL9),  or  First-professional(LEVEL10) degrees, or certificates above the baccalaureate level(LEVEL6,LEVEL8 and LEVEL11). They do offer postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year (LEVEL1); at least one but less than two academic years (LEVEL2); or at least two but less than four academic years.(LEVEL4) (IC)

All inactive institutions (CYACTIVE in (2,3)) and administrative units (Sector=0) were coded as not applicable. Any institution that did not respond to the 2006-07 Institutional Characteristics component or the 2005-06 Completions component were coded as not reported or could not derive. These were all NonTitle IV institutions.

Additional notes on classifying Degree-granting primarily baccalaureate or above and other baccalaureate granting:

Degree-granting institutions whose completions data are reported with their parent institution were assigned the same code as the parent institution.
 
New degree-granting institutions that offer a bachelor's degree, but have not yet awarded bachelor degrees in academic year 2005-06 were assigned as follows:

  If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above (indicating the level was offered) and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above.
  
  If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's degree and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, other baccalaureate granting.
  
  For institutions that reported zeros for both bachelor's degrees or above and for levels below the bachelor's the number of programs (CIP codes) by level was used to determine the primary classification. If the number of programs with reported zeros for degrees/certificates at the bachelor's level or above was greater than the number of programs with reported zeros for degrees/certificates less than the baccalaureate, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, primarily bachelor's or above.  If the number of programs with reported zeros for degrees/certificates at the bachelor's level or above was less than the number of programs with reported zeros for degrees/certificates less than the baccalaureate, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, other baccalaureate granting.

codes.1: Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees
codes.2: Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above
codes.3: Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above
codes.5: Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate
codes.6: Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate

title: Institutional category
description:
Institutional category was derived using the level of offerings reported on the Institutional Characteristics (IC) component and the number and level of awards that were reported on the Completions (C) component.

Category descriptions:

1) Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees - These institutions offer a Master's degree, Doctor's degree  or a First-professional degree and do not offer a Bachelor's degree or an Associate's degree. 

2) Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree,Doctor's degree or a First-professional degree.  Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded is greater than 50 percent. 

3) Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree, Doctor's degree,or a First-professional degree.  Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded must be less than or equal to 50 percent.

4) Degree-granting, Associate's and certificates - Institutions offer an Associate's degree and may offer other postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year; at least one but less-than two academic years; at least two but less-than four academic years. This category also includes institutions that offer a postbaccalaureate certificate, Post-master's certificate or a First-professional certificate and the highest degree offered is an Associate's degree.

5) Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctor's or First-professional degrees, but offer either Postbaccaulaureate, Post-master's or First-professional certificates. 

6) Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's, Bachelor's , Master's, Doctor's, or First-professional degrees, or certificates above the baccalaureate level. They do offer postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year; at least one but less than two academic years; or at least two but less than four academic years.

Technical details for Institutional Category (INSTCAT):

Total degrees and certificates and total bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree awarded are derived using data from the Completions component.

Total bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree is the sum of: 

Bachelor's degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=5,MAJORNUM=1)
Postbaccalaureate certificates (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=6,MAJORNUM=1)
Master's degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=7,MAJORNUM=1)
Post-master's certificates (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=8,MAJORNUM=1)
Doctor's degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=9,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=10,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional certificates (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=11,MAJORNUM=1)

Total degrees and certificates is the sum of Bachelor degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelors degree as defined above added to the following:

Associate's degrees (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=3,MAJORNUM=1)
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least two but less-than four academic years 
   (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=4, MAJORNUM=1).
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least one but less-than two academic years
   (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=2,MAJORNUM=1); 
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year 
    (CRACE24,AWLEVEL=1,MAJORNUM=1) 

Institutions are classified as Degree-granting (DEGGRANT=1) or Nondegree-granting(DEGGRANT=2) using level of offerings data reported on the Institutional Characteristics component. Degree-granting institutions offer an Associate's (LEVEL3=1),Bachelor's (LEVEL5=1, Master's (LEVEL7=1), Doctoral (LEVEL9=1), or a First-Professional (LEVEL10=1) degree. Any institution that offers only certificates are Nondegree-granting.

Nondegree-granting institutions that offer a postbaccalaureate certificate (LEVEL6=1) or a post-master's certificate (LEVEL8=1) or a First-professional certificate (LEVEL11=1) are classified as Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate (INSTCAT=5).

Nondegree-granting institutions that only offer certificates of less-than four academic years are classified as Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate (INSTCAT=6).

Degree-granting institutions whose highest degree granted are Associate's (HDEGOFFR=40) are classified as Degree-granting, Associate's and certificates (INSTCAT=4). (There are a few 4-year institutions that grant Postbaccalaureate or Post-master's or First-professional certificates in this category).

Degree-granting institutions that do not grant a Bachelor's degree (LEVEL5=0) and do not grant an Associate's degree (LEVEL3=0) are classified as Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees (INSTCAT=1).

The remaining degree-granting institutions offer a bachelor's degree or an associate's degree, or both.
For these institutions a percent of bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree of  total degrees and certificates is generated. If the percent is greater than 50, institutions are classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above (INSTCAT=2), If the percent is 50 or less, institutions are classified as Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above (INSTCAT=3).

Inactive institutions (CYACTIVE in (2,3)) and administrative units (Sector=0) were coded as not applicable. All Non-Title IV institutions that did not respond to the  IC or Completions components were coded as not reported. 
Degree-granting institutions whose completions data are reported with their parent institution were assigned the same code as the parent institution.
New degree-granting institutions that report offering a bachelor's degree on the current institutional characteristics file for the upcoming academic year, and have not yet reported bachelor's degrees on the current completions that covers the previous academic year  June 1-July 30 were assigned as follows:

If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above (indicating the level was offered) and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above. If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's degree and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above.

For institutions that reported zeros for bachelor's degrees of above and for levels below the bachelor's, the maximum number of programs by level was used to determine the primary classification.

codes.1: Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees
codes.2: Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above
codes.3: Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above
codes.5: Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate
codes.6: Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate

title: Postsecondary and Title IV institution indicator
description:
A derived indicator to easily select institutions who are (1) currently in the IPEDS universe, (2) open to the public, (3) participant in Title IV program, and (4) primarily postsecondary institution.

This variable is used to produce tables that are published in IPEDS E.D. tabs and tables in the Digest of Education Statistics.

It is derived as follows:
If opeflag in (1 2 ) and deggrant in (1 2) and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=1
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and deggrant in (1 2) and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=2
If opeflag in (1 2 ) and deggrant in (3) and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=3
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and deggrant in (3) and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=4
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and deggrant in (1 2) and openpubl=2 then pset4flg=6
If cyactive=2 then pset4flg=9
The four United States Service Air Force, Coast Guard, Naval and Military Academies are also included as PSET4FLG=1, even though they are opeflag=3, deferment only.

codes.1: Title IV postsecondary institution
codes.2: Non-Title IV postsecondary institution
codes.3: Title IV NOT primarily postsecondary institution
codes.4: Non-Title IV NOT primarily postsecondary institution
codes.6: Non-Title IV postsecondary institution that is NOT open to the public
codes.9: Institution is not active in current universe

title: Institutional category
description:
Institutional category was derived using the level of offerings reported on the Institutional Characteristics (IC) component and the number and level of awards that were reported on the Completions (C) component.

Category descriptions:

1) Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees - These institutions offer a Master's degree, Doctor's degree  or a First-professional degree and do not offer a Bachelor's degree or an Associate's degree. 

2) Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree,Doctor's degree or a First-professional degree.  Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded is greater than 50 percent. 

3) Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree, Doctor's degree,or a First-professional degree.  Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded must be less than or equal to 50 percent.

4) Degree-granting, Associate's and certificates - Institutions offer an Associate's degree and may offer other postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year; at least one but less-than two academic years; at least two but less-than four academic years. This category also includes institutions that offer a postbaccalaureate certificate, Post-master's certificate or a First-professional certificate and the highest degree offered is an Associate's degree.

5) Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctor's or First-professional degrees, but offer either Postbaccaulaureate, Post-master's or First-professional certificates. 

6) Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's, Bachelor's , Master's, Doctor's, or First-professional degrees, or certificates above the baccalaureate level. They do offer postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year; at least one but less than two academic years; or at least two but less than four academic years.

Technical details for Institutional Category (INSTCAT):

Total degrees and certificates and total bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree awarded are derived using data from the Completions component.

Total bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree is the sum of: 

Bachelor's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=5,MAJORNUM=1)
Postbaccalaureate certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=6,MAJORNUM=1)
Master's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=7,MAJORNUM=1)
Post-master's certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=8,MAJORNUM=1)
Doctor's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=9,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=10,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=11,MAJORNUM=1)

Total degrees and certificates is the sum of Bachelor degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelors degree as defined above added to the following:

Associate's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=3,MAJORNUM=1)
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least two but less-than four academic years 
   (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=4, MAJORNUM=1).
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least one but less-than two academic years
   (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=2,MAJORNUM=1); 
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year 
    (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=1,MAJORNUM=1) 

Institutions are classified as Degree-granting (DEGGRANT=1) or Nondegree-granting(DEGGRANT=2) using level of offerings data reported on the Institutional Characteristics component. Degree-granting institutions offer an Associate's (LEVEL3=1),Bachelor's (LEVEL5=1, Master's (LEVEL7=1), Doctoral (LEVEL9=1), or a First-Professional (LEVEL10=1) degree. Any institution that offers only certificates are Nondegree-granting.

Nondegree-granting institutions that offer a postbaccalaureate certificate (LEVEL6=1) or a post-master's certificate (LEVEL8=1) or a First-professional certificate (LEVEL11=1) are classified as Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate (INSTCAT=5).

Nondegree-granting institutions that only offer certificates of less-than four academic years are classified as Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate (INSTCAT=6).

Degree-granting institutions whose highest degree granted are Associate's (HDEGOFFR=40) are classified as Degree-granting, Associate's and certificates (INSTCAT=4). (There are a few 4-year institutions that grant Postbaccalaureate or Post-master's or First-professional certificates in this category).

Degree-granting institutions that do not grant a Bachelor's degree (LEVEL5=0) and do not grant an Associate's degree (LEVEL3=0) are classified as Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees (INSTCAT=1).

The remaining degree-granting institutions offer a bachelor's degree or an associate's degree, or both.
For these institutions a percent of bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree of  total degrees and certificates is generated. If the percent is greater than 50, institutions are classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above (INSTCAT=2), If the percent is 50 or less, institutions are classified as Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above (INSTCAT=3).

Inactive institutions (CYACTIVE in (2,3)) and administrative units (Sector=0) were coded as not applicable. All Non-Title IV institutions that did not respond to the  IC or Completions components were coded as not reported. 
Degree-granting institutions whose completions data are reported with their parent institution were assigned the same code as the parent institution.
New degree-granting institutions that report offering a bachelor's degree on the current institutional characteristics file for the upcoming academic year, and have not yet reported bachelor's degrees on the current completions that covers the previous academic year  June 1-July 30 were assigned as follows:

If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above (indicating the level was offered) and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above. If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's degree and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above.

For institutions that reported zeros for bachelor's degrees of above and for levels below the bachelor's, the maximum number of programs by level was used to determine the primary classification.

codes.1: Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees
codes.2: Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above
codes.3: Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above
codes.5: Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate
codes.6: Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate

title: Institutional category
description:
Institutional category was derived using the level of offerings reported on the Institutional Characteristics (IC) component and the number and level of awards that were reported on the Completions (C) component.

Category descriptions:

1) Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees - These institutions offer a Master's degree, Doctor's degree  or a First-professional degree and do not offer a Bachelor's degree or an Associate's degree. 

2) Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree,Doctor's degree or a First-professional degree.  Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded is greater than 50 percent. 

3) Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree, Doctor's degree,or a First-professional degree.  Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded must be less than or equal to 50 percent.

4) Degree-granting, Associate's and certificates - Institutions offer an Associate's degree and may offer other postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year; at least one but less-than two academic years; at least two but less-than four academic years. This category also includes institutions that offer a postbaccalaureate certificate, Post-master's certificate or a First-professional certificate and the highest degree offered is an Associate's degree.

5) Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctor's or First-professional degrees, but offer either Postbaccaulaureate, Post-master's or First-professional certificates. 

6) Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's, Bachelor's , Master's, Doctor's, or First-professional degrees, or certificates above the baccalaureate level. They do offer postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year; at least one but less than two academic years; or at least two but less than four academic years.

Technical details for Institutional Category (INSTCAT):

Total degrees and certificates and total bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree awarded are derived using data from the Completions component.

Total bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree is the sum of: 

Bachelor's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=5,MAJORNUM=1)
Postbaccalaureate certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=6,MAJORNUM=1)
Master's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=7,MAJORNUM=1)
Post-master's certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=8,MAJORNUM=1)
Doctor's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=9,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=10,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=11,MAJORNUM=1)

Total degrees and certificates is the sum of Bachelor degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelors degree as defined above added to the following:

Associate's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=3,MAJORNUM=1)
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least two but less-than four academic years 
   (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=4, MAJORNUM=1).
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least one but less-than two academic years
   (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=2,MAJORNUM=1); 
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year 
    (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=1,MAJORNUM=1) 

Institutions are classified as Degree-granting (DEGGRANT=1) or Nondegree-granting(DEGGRANT=2) using level of offerings data reported on the Institutional Characteristics component. Degree-granting institutions offer an Associate's (LEVEL3=1),Bachelor's (LEVEL5=1, Master's (LEVEL7=1), Doctoral (LEVEL9=1), or a First-Professional (LEVEL10=1) degree. Any institution that offers only certificates are Nondegree-granting.

Nondegree-granting institutions that offer a postbaccalaureate certificate (LEVEL6=1) or a post-master's certificate (LEVEL8=1) or a First-professional certificate (LEVEL11=1) are classified as Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate (INSTCAT=5).

Nondegree-granting institutions that only offer certificates of less-than four academic years are classified as Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate (INSTCAT=6).

Degree-granting institutions whose highest degree granted are Associate's (HDEGOFFR=40) are classified as Degree-granting, Associate's and certificates (INSTCAT=4). (There are a few 4-year institutions that grant Postbaccalaureate or Post-master's or First-professional certificates in this category).

Degree-granting institutions that do not grant a Bachelor's degree (LEVEL5=0) and do not grant an Associate's degree (LEVEL3=0) are classified as Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees (INSTCAT=1).

The remaining degree-granting institutions offer a bachelor's degree or an associate's degree, or both.
For these institutions a percent of bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree of  total degrees and certificates is generated. If the percent is greater than 50, institutions are classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above (INSTCAT=2), If the percent is 50 or less, institutions are classified as Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above (INSTCAT=3).

Inactive institutions (CYACTIVE in (2,3)) and administrative units (Sector=0) were coded as not applicable. All Non-Title IV institutions that did not respond to the  IC or Completions components were coded as not reported. 
Degree-granting institutions whose completions data are reported with their parent institution were assigned the same code as the parent institution.
New degree-granting institutions that report offering a bachelor's degree on the current institutional characteristics file for the upcoming academic year, and have not yet reported bachelor's degrees on the current completions that covers the previous academic year  June 1-July 30 were assigned as follows:

If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above (indicating the level was offered) and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above. If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's degree and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above.

For institutions that reported zeros for bachelor's degrees of above and for levels below the bachelor's, the maximum number of programs by level was used to determine the primary classification.

Master's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=7,MAJORNUM=1)
Post-master's certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=8,MAJORNUM=1)
Doctor's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=9,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=10,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=11,MAJORNUM=1)

title: Institutional category
description:
Institutional category was derived using the level of offerings reported on the Institutional Characteristics (IC) component and the number and level of awards that were reported on the Completions (C) component.

Category descriptions:

1) Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees - These institutions offer a Master's degree, Doctor's degree  or a First-professional degree and do not offer a Bachelor's degree or an Associate's degree. 

2) Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree,Doctor's degree or a First-professional degree.  Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded is greater than 50 percent. 

3) Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree, Doctor's degree,or a First-professional degree.  Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded must be less than or equal to 50 percent.

4) Degree-granting, Associate's and certificates - Institutions offer an Associate's degree and may offer other postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year; at least one but less-than two academic years; at least two but less-than four academic years. This category also includes institutions that offer a postbaccalaureate certificate, Post-master's certificate or a First-professional certificate and the highest degree offered is an Associate's degree.

5) Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctor's or First-professional degrees, but offer either Postbaccaulaureate, Post-master's or First-professional certificates. 

6) Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's, Bachelor's , Master's, Doctor's, or First-professional degrees, or certificates above the baccalaureate level. They do offer postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year; at least one but less than two academic years; or at least two but less than four academic years.

Technical details for Institutional Category (INSTCAT):

Total degrees and certificates and total bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree awarded are derived using data from the Completions component.

Total bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree is the sum of: 

Bachelor's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=5,MAJORNUM=1)
Postbaccalaureate certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=6,MAJORNUM=1)
Master's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=7,MAJORNUM=1)
Post-master's certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=8,MAJORNUM=1)
Doctor's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=9,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=10,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=11,MAJORNUM=1)

Total degrees and certificates is the sum of Bachelor degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelors degree as defined above added to the following:

Associate's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=3,MAJORNUM=1)
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least two but less-than four academic years 
   (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=4, MAJORNUM=1).
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least one but less-than two academic years
   (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=2,MAJORNUM=1); 
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year 
    (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=1,MAJORNUM=1) 

Institutions are classified as Degree-granting (DEGGRANT=1) or Nondegree-granting(DEGGRANT=2) using level of offerings data reported on the Institutional Characteristics component. Degree-granting institutions offer an Associate's (LEVEL3=1),Bachelor's (LEVEL5=1, Master's (LEVEL7=1), Doctoral (LEVEL9=1), or a First-Professional (LEVEL10=1) degree. Any institution that offers only certificates are Nondegree-granting.

Nondegree-granting institutions that offer a postbaccalaureate certificate (LEVEL6=1) or a post-master's certificate (LEVEL8=1) or a First-professional certificate (LEVEL11=1) are classified as Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate (INSTCAT=5).

Nondegree-granting institutions that only offer certificates of less-than four academic years are classified as Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate (INSTCAT=6).

Degree-granting institutions whose highest degree granted are Associate's (HDEGOFFR=40) are classified as Degree-granting, Associate's and certificates (INSTCAT=4). (There are a few 4-year institutions that grant Postbaccalaureate or Post-master's or First-professional certificates in this category).

Degree-granting institutions that do not grant a Bachelor's degree (LEVEL5=0) and do not grant an Associate's degree (LEVEL3=0) are classified as Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees (INSTCAT=1).

The remaining degree-granting institutions offer a bachelor's degree or an associate's degree, or both.
For these institutions a percent of bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree of  total degrees and certificates is generated. If the percent is greater than 50, institutions are classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above (INSTCAT=2), If the percent is 50 or less, institutions are classified as Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above (INSTCAT=3).

Inactive institutions (CYACTIVE in (2,3)) and administrative units (Sector=0) were coded as not applicable. All Non-Title IV institutions that did not respond to the  IC or Completions components were coded as not reported. 
Degree-granting institutions whose completions data are reported with their parent institution were assigned the same code as the parent institution.
New degree-granting institutions that report offering a bachelor's degree on the current institutional characteristics file for the upcoming academic year, and have not yet reported bachelor's degrees on the current completions that covers the previous academic year  June 1-July 30 were assigned as follows:

If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above (indicating the level was offered) and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above. If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's degree and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above.

For institutions that reported zeros for bachelor's degrees of above and for levels below the bachelor's, the maximum number of programs by level was used to determine the primary classification.

title: Institutional category
description:
Institutional category was derived using the level of offerings reported on the Institutional Characteristics (IC) component and the number and level of awards that were reported on the Completions (C) component.

Category descriptions:

1) Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees - These institutions offer a Master's degree, Doctor's degree  or a First-professional degree and do not offer a Bachelor's degree or an Associate's degree. 

2) Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree,Doctor's degree or a First-professional degree.  Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded is greater than 50 percent. 

3) Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree, Doctor's degree,or a First-professional degree.  Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded must be less than or equal to 50 percent.

4) Degree-granting, Associate's and certificates - Institutions offer an Associate's degree and may offer other postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year; at least one but less-than two academic years; at least two but less-than four academic years. This category also includes institutions that offer a postbaccalaureate certificate, Post-master's certificate or a First-professional certificate and the highest degree offered is an Associate's degree.

5) Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctor's or First-professional degrees, but offer either Postbaccaulaureate, Post-master's or First-professional certificates. 

6) Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's, Bachelor's , Master's, Doctor's, or First-professional degrees, or certificates above the baccalaureate level. They do offer postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year; at least one but less than two academic years; or at least two but less than four academic years.

Technical details for Institutional Category (INSTCAT):

Total degrees and certificates and total bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree awarded are derived using data from the Completions component.

Total bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree is the sum of: 

Bachelor's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=5,MAJORNUM=1)
Postbaccalaureate certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=6,MAJORNUM=1)
Master's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=7,MAJORNUM=1)
Post-master's certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=8,MAJORNUM=1)
Doctor's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=9,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=10,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=11,MAJORNUM=1)

Total degrees and certificates is the sum of Bachelor degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelors degree as defined above added to the following:

Associate's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=3,MAJORNUM=1)
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least two but less-than four academic years 
   (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=4, MAJORNUM=1).
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least one but less-than two academic years
   (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=2,MAJORNUM=1); 
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year 
    (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=1,MAJORNUM=1) 

Institutions are classified as Degree-granting (DEGGRANT=1) or Nondegree-granting(DEGGRANT=2) using level of offerings data reported on the Institutional Characteristics component. Degree-granting institutions offer an Associate's (LEVEL3=1),Bachelor's (LEVEL5=1, Master's (LEVEL7=1), Doctoral (LEVEL9=1), or a First-Professional (LEVEL10=1) degree. Any institution that offers only certificates are Nondegree-granting.

Nondegree-granting institutions that offer a postbaccalaureate certificate (LEVEL6=1) or a post-master's certificate (LEVEL8=1) or a First-professional certificate (LEVEL11=1) are classified as Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate (INSTCAT=5).

Nondegree-granting institutions that only offer certificates of less-than four academic years are classified as Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate (INSTCAT=6).

Degree-granting institutions whose highest degree granted are Associate's (HDEGOFFR=40) are classified as Degree-granting, Associate's and certificates (INSTCAT=4). (There are a few 4-year institutions that grant Postbaccalaureate or Post-master's or First-professional certificates in this category).

Degree-granting institutions that do not grant a Bachelor's degree (LEVEL5=0) and do not grant an Associate's degree (LEVEL3=0) are classified as Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees (INSTCAT=1).

The remaining degree-granting institutions offer a bachelor's degree or an associate's degree, or both.
For these institutions a percent of bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree of  total degrees and certificates is generated. If the percent is greater than 50, institutions are classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above (INSTCAT=2), If the percent is 50 or less, institutions are classified as Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above (INSTCAT=3).

Inactive institutions (CYACTIVE in (2,3)) and administrative units (Sector=0) were coded as not applicable. All Non-Title IV institutions that did not respond to the  IC or Completions components were coded as not reported. 
Degree-granting institutions whose completions data are reported with their parent institution were assigned the same code as the parent institution.
New degree-granting institutions that report offering a bachelor's degree on the current institutional characteristics file for the upcoming academic year, and have not yet reported bachelor's degrees on the current completions that covers the previous academic year  June 1-July 30 were assigned as follows:

If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above (indicating the level was offered) and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above. If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's degree and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above.

For institutions that reported zeros for bachelor's degrees of above and for levels below the bachelor's, the maximum number of programs by level was used to determine the primary classification.

codes.2: Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above
codes.3: Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above
codes.5: Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate
codes.6: Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate

title: Postsecondary and Title IV institution indicator
description:
A derived indicator to easily select institutions who are (1) currently in the IPEDS universe, (2) open to the public, (3) participant in Title IV program, and (4) primarily postsecondary institution.

This variable is used to produce tables that are published in IPEDS First look reports(previously known as E.D. tabs) and tables in the Digest of Education Statistics.
The  "First Look" universe of institutitons includes Title IV primarily postsecondary and Title IV not primarily postsecondary institutions ( PSET4FLG in (1,3)).  Prior to IPEDS 2010 data collection the "First Look/E.D. Tabs" universe included Title IV  primarily postsecondary institutions ( PSET4FLG =1). 

It is derived as follows:
If opeflag in (1 2 7 ) and pseflag=1 and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=1
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and pseflag=1 and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=2
If opeflag in (1 2 7) and  pseflag=2 and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=3
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and pseflag=2 and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=4
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and pseflag=1 and openpubl=2 then pset4flg=6
If cyactive=2 then pset4flg=9
The  United States  Air Force, Naval and  Military Academies  are also included as PSET4FLG=1, even though they are opeflag=3, deferment only. The United States Coast Guard, a nonTitle iv school (OPEFLAG=5)  is also included .

codes.1: Title IV postsecondary institution
codes.2: Non-Title IV postsecondary institution
codes.3: Title IV NOT primarily postsecondary institution
codes.6: Non-Title IV postsecondary institution that is NOT open to the public
codes.9: Institution is not active in current universe

title: Institutional category
description:
Institutional category was derived using the level of offerings reported on the Institutional Characteristics (IC) component and the number and level of awards that were reported on the Completions (C) component.

Category descriptions:

1) Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees - These institutions offer a Master's degree, Doctor's degree  or a First-professional degree and do not offer a Bachelor's degree or an Associate's degree. 

2) Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree,Doctor's degree or a First-professional degree.  Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded is greater than 50 percent. 

3) Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above - These institutions offer a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree, Doctor's degree,or a First-professional degree.  Also, the total number of degrees/certificates at or above the bachelor's level awarded divided by the total number of degrees/certificates awarded must be less than or equal to 50 percent.

4) Degree-granting, Associate's and certificates - Institutions offer an Associate's degree and may offer other postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year; at least one but less-than two academic years; at least two but less-than four academic years. This category also includes institutions that offer a postbaccalaureate certificate, Post-master's certificate or a First-professional certificate and the highest degree offered is an Associate's degree.

5) Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctor's or First-professional degrees, but offer either Postbaccaulaureate, Post-master's or First-professional certificates. 

6) Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate - Institutions do not offer Associate's, Bachelor's , Master's, Doctor's, or First-professional degrees, or certificates above the baccalaureate level. They do offer postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year; at least one but less than two academic years; or at least two but less than four academic years.

Technical details for Institutional Category (INSTCAT):

Total degrees and certificates and total bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree awarded are derived using data from the Completions component.

Total bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree is the sum of: 

Bachelor's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=5,MAJORNUM=1)
Postbaccalaureate certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=6,MAJORNUM=1)
Master's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=7,MAJORNUM=1)
Post-master's certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=8,MAJORNUM=1)
Doctor's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=9,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=10,MAJORNUM=1)
First-professional certificates (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=11,MAJORNUM=1)

Total degrees and certificates is the sum of Bachelor degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelors degree as defined above added to the following:

Associate's degrees (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=3,MAJORNUM=1)
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least two but less-than four academic years 
   (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=4, MAJORNUM=1).
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of at least one but less-than two academic years
   (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=2,MAJORNUM=1); 
Postsecondary certificates, awards or diplomas of less than one academic year 
    (CTOTALT,AWLEVEL=1,MAJORNUM=1) 

Institutions are classified as Degree-granting (DEGGRANT=1) or Nondegree-granting(DEGGRANT=2) using level of offerings data reported on the Institutional Characteristics component. Degree-granting institutions offer an Associate's (LEVEL3=1),Bachelor's (LEVEL5=1, Master's (LEVEL7=1), Doctoral (LEVEL9=1), or a First-Professional (LEVEL10=1) degree. Any institution that offers only certificates are Nondegree-granting.

Nondegree-granting institutions that offer a postbaccalaureate certificate (LEVEL6=1) or a post-master's certificate (LEVEL8=1) or a First-professional certificate (LEVEL11=1) are classified as Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate (INSTCAT=5).

Nondegree-granting institutions that only offer certificates of less-than four academic years are classified as Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate (INSTCAT=6).

Degree-granting institutions whose highest degree granted are Associate's (HDEGOFFR=40) are classified as Degree-granting, Associate's and certificates (INSTCAT=4). (There are a few 4-year institutions that grant Postbaccalaureate or Post-master's or First-professional certificates in this category).

Degree-granting institutions that do not grant a Bachelor's degree (LEVEL5=0) and do not grant an Associate's degree (LEVEL3=0) are classified as Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees (INSTCAT=1).

The remaining degree-granting institutions offer a bachelor's degree or an associate's degree, or both.
For these institutions a percent of bachelor's degrees and all other degrees/certificates above the bachelor's degree of  total degrees and certificates is generated. If the percent is greater than 50, institutions are classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above (INSTCAT=2), If the percent is 50 or less, institutions are classified as Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above (INSTCAT=3).

Inactive institutions (CYACTIVE in (2,3)) and administrative units (Sector=0) were coded as not applicable. All Non-Title IV institutions that did not respond to the  IC or Completions components were coded as not reported. 
Degree-granting institutions whose completions data are reported with their parent institution were assigned the same code as the parent institution.
New degree-granting institutions that report offering a bachelor's degree on the current institutional characteristics file for the upcoming academic year, and have not yet reported bachelor's degrees on the current completions that covers the previous academic year  June 1-July 30 were assigned as follows:

If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above (indicating the level was offered) and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above. If an institution reported a zero in any program (CIP code) at any level below the bachelor's degree and did not report a zero for any program (CIP code) for bachelor's degrees or above, the institution was classified as Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above.

For institutions that reported zeros for bachelor's degrees of above and for levels below the bachelor's, the maximum number of programs by level was used to determine the primary classification.

codes.1: Degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees
codes.2: Degree-granting, primarily baccalaureate or above
codes.3: Degree-granting, not primarily baccalaureate or above
codes.5: Nondegree-granting, above the baccalaureate
codes.6: Nondegree-granting, sub-baccalaureate

title: Postsecondary and Title IV institution indicator
description:
A derived indicator to easily select institutions who are (1) currently in the IPEDS universe, (2) open to the public, (3) participant in Title IV program, and (4) primarily postsecondary institution.

This variable is used to produce tables that are published in IPEDS First look reports(previously known as E.D. tabs) and tables in the Digest of Education Statistics.
The  "First Look" universe of institutitons includes Title IV primarily postsecondary and Title IV not primarily postsecondary institutions ( PSET4FLG in (1,3)).  Prior to IPEDS 2010 data collection the "First Look/E.D. Tabs" universe included Title IV  primarily postsecondary institutions ( PSET4FLG =1). 

It is derived as follows:
If opeflag in (1 2 7 ) and pseflag=1 and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=1
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and pseflag=1 and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=2
If opeflag in (1 2 7) and  pseflag=2 and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=3
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and pseflag=2 and openpubl=1 then pset4flg=4
If opeflag in (3 4 5 6) and pseflag=1 and openpubl=2 then pset4flg=6
If cyactive=2 then pset4flg=9
The  United States  Air Force, Naval and  Military Academies  are also included as PSET4FLG=1, even though they are opeflag=3, deferment only. The United States Coast Guard, a nonTitle iv school (OPEFLAG=5)  is also included .

codes.1: Title IV postsecondary institution
codes.2: Non-Title IV postsecondary institution
codes.3: Title IV NOT primarily postsecondary institution
codes.4: Non-Title IV NOT primarily postsecondary institution
codes.6: Non-Title IV postsecondary institution that is NOT open to the public
codes.9: Institution is not active in current universe
